acceptanceCriteria: Recognizably belongs to the Giants family and preserves every identity invariant.
Reads specifically as Mountain Lord, T4, rather than another family form.
Communicates the Watershed Route Commander (Champion) archetype and its battlefield duty.
Preserves coherent load-bearing anatomy, complete limbs, and believable ground contact.
Uses at least two water construction dimensions without a palette-only or glow-only treatment.
Keeps the attack telegraph and counterplay signal visible at gameplay scale.
Frames one complete featured subject with no crop, labels, UI text, or watermark.
Output remains a candidate until independent approved-review evidence exists; it is never a runtime asset.
anatomyInvariants: Mountain-tall, with waterfalls running from the shoulders, pines rooted in the crags of the back, and iron rings the size of gates set among mature stone shelves.

Signature mechanic: Three Watersheds: the Mountain Lord turns one gate-sized iron ring at its waist to open a shoulder fall, tilts a pine-crag to release scree across a second route, and points lower forms toward the third. The Lord must brace both arms against the terrain while changing the watershed, exposing a runed sternum shelf.
battlefieldDuty: Control multiple terrain routes by opening shoulder waterfalls, dropping pine-marked scree, and assigning lower Giants to exploit the dry route that remains.
constructionDimensions: Body geology becomes a watershed system of saturated moss terraces, ice-braced stone, carved runoff channels, hanging pools, and chain-linked spill gates across recognizable skin and rock plates.
Surface and motion show coherent volume through wet reflections, visibly filling basins, pressure-fed falls, calving ice shelves, and drainage that changes the Giant's balance as reservoirs empty.
counterplay: Follow the bending pines to the route that will stay dry, redirect a Hill Giant roll into the selected ring, or climb the grounded arm and strike the sternum rune while both hands manage the watershed. Affinity signal: A shoulder basin overtops and a spill gate strains before a water-driven action; opening the gate early or cracking its ice brace drains the loaded side and exposes the dry binding joint.
forbiddenTreatments: Palette-only water treatment without watershed construction, saturation, and changed weight distribution
Glow-only water treatment without reservoirs, coherent drainage, or wet surface response
Shapeless water anatomy that replaces the Giant's skin, stone growth, or joints
Mist or waterfalls that conceal paths, anchors, or spill-gate counterplay
identityInvariants: Humanlike proportions scaled upward with a heavy brow, thick limbs, dense bone, and a slight stoop that communicates the body's own weight.
Stone gray, granite blue-gray, earth brown, moss green, glacier white, and warm amber eyes remain the family palette without requiring an elemental origin.
Rough hide, raw stone, moss, lichen, pine, iron chain, and rope accumulate as bodily geology and oversized practical tools.
Chains, standing-stone jewelry, skin runes, and whole trees function as ornament at a scale that stays legible from the arena.
Raw scale and geological coverage escalate together until the Sovereign carries a valley, but every form retains recognizable humanoid load paths and slow committed motion.
telegraph: Pines bend toward one back crag, one waterfall narrows to a suspended sheet, and the selected iron ring groans as both massive hands reach for the landscape.
